caption: Within-compound variation and estimated variance fractions. A: Measurements are centred on each compound's mean. Facets distinguish compounds measured repeatedly within one source from compounds measured across multiple sources. Points represent measurements and vertical lines show ranges. Compounds are ranked by observed range within each facet. Both facets use the same vertical scale. Observed ranges depend on measurement counts and do not by themselves establish a source effect. B: Variance fractions from the full pooled dataset using an intercept-only REML model with compound and source random intercepts, without molecular descriptors or temperature. Labels show estimated percentages with marginal 95% parametric bootstrap confidence intervals in brackets. Source denotes the original publication. Source-associated variance does not identify experimental causes.

One-anchor calibration for held-out sources, evaluated on compounds absent from training. RMSE decrease is uncalibrated minus calibrated RMSE. Positive values indicate improvement and negative values indicate worsening. Performance was averaged across every available single anchor within each source. Horizontal lines connect estimates to zero and are not confidence intervals. The teal dashed line shows the mean RMSE decrease across all sources, giving equal weight to each source. Sources are ordered by RMSE decrease. RMSE is expressed in log10 Kp units, with Kp in cm/h. Source identities are provided in Additional file 1.

Calibration benefit from zero to five anchors within the fixed subset. Zero anchors represents uncalibrated predictions. RMSE decrease is uncalibrated minus calibrated RMSE. Thin lines show individual sources. Red lines identify sources that worsened from one to five anchors. The blue line shows the mean decrease with equal source weighting. Shading shows pointwise 95% source-bootstrap confidence intervals relative to no calibration. The annotated additional decrease and its confidence interval compare one with five anchors. Performance averages all possible panels within each source and anchor count. The sources and test measurements remain fixed. RMSE is expressed in log10 Kp units, with Kp in cm/h. Source identities are provided in Additional file 1.

One- and five-anchor calibration in two sources. Points show mean estimated offsets and grey lines show full ranges across all possible panels, not confidence intervals. Red dashed lines show the mean uncalibrated test residuals, which minimize test RMSE among constant offsets. These benchmarks were calculated retrospectively and were not used for calibration. The numerical column shows mean calibrated RMSE across panels. Zero on the adjustment axis represents no correction. Both examples use the same adjustment scale. Panels can share compounds and are not independent experiments. Offsets and RMSE are expressed in log10 Kp units, with Kp in cm/h. Red RMSE values indicate higher error with five anchors than with one. The estimated correction points in the wrong direction in A and is too large in B. In both examples, five anchors narrow the offset range but increase mean RMSE.

One-anchor calibration diagnostics across eligible sources. Points show mean offsets and vertical lines show full ranges across all available single anchors. Ranges are not confidence intervals. The dashed diagonal indicates equality between the estimated offset and mean uncalibrated test residual. Colours indicate the change in mean RMSE across single anchors. Both axes are expressed in log10 Kp units. Test residuals were calculated retrospectively. Mean offsets alone do not determine mean RMSE because offsets vary among anchor choices.
Calibration effects and 95% publication-bootstrap intervals under each curation policy. Evaluation populations and test measurements can differ between policies.
Pooled variance fractions and 95% parametric-bootstrap intervals from the intercept-only crossed random-intercept model. Intervals are marginal and their bounds do not sum to 100%.
